classification.difficultyReason: Model grazing as a quadrant clipped by field boundaries, construct sector-minus-triangle corrections, and establish that the two excluded regions do not overlap.

content.prompt: A goat is tied by a rope to a corner of a grassy field of width 30 metres and length 40 metres.

spec.description: Unfilled rectangular field with bottom and right dimension labels; rope connects the lower-right tether point to an interior goat position marker. The illustrative goat position and rope curve are not numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Rectangular field 40 m by 30 m; tether at the lower-right corner.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied dimensions and tether relationship are visible.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What length of rope would ensure that the goat can access all of the grass in the field?

answer.worked:
The opposite corner is the farthest point from the tether.
$$\begin{align*}L^2&=30^2+40^2\\L^2&=2500\\L&=50\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What percentage of the field’s area can the goat access if the length of the rope is 30 metres? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
The accessible region is a quadrant of radius $30\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{field}}&=30\times40=1200\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{accessible}}&=\frac14\pi(30)^2=225\pi\text{ m}^2\\\text{Percentage}&=\frac{225\pi}{1200}\times100\\\text{Percentage}&\approx58.90\%.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What percentage of the field’s area can the goat access if the length of the rope is 35 metres? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$75.09\%$

Subtract the circular segment beyond the 30 m boundary from the quadrant.
answer.worked:
Subtract the segment extending beyond the 30 m boundary. Let $\alpha$ be the angle between the perpendicular to that boundary and the radius to its intersection with the circle; let $s$ be the distance along the boundary from the perpendicular foot to that intersection.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{30}{35}\right)\\s&=\sqrt{35^2-30^2}=5\sqrt{13}\text{ m}\\A_{\text{segment}}&=\frac{\alpha}{360^{\circ}}\pi(35)^2-\frac12(30)(5\sqrt{13})\\A_{\text{accessible}}&=\frac14\pi(35)^2-A_{\text{segment}}\\A_{\text{accessible}}&\approx901.105636\text{ m}^2\\\text{Percentage}&=\frac{A_{\text{accessible}}}{1200}\times100\\\text{Percentage}&\approx75.09\%.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: What percentage of the field’s area can the goat access if the length of the rope is 45 metres? Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$97.70\%$

Subtract the two circular segments beyond the 30 m and 40 m boundaries from the quadrant.
answer.worked:
The quadrant extends beyond both boundaries. The two outside segments do not overlap because the opposite corner is $50\text{ m}$ from the tether. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the angles between the perpendiculars to the respective boundaries and the radii to their circle intersections.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{30}{45}\right)\\\beta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{40}{45}\right)\\s_{30}&=\sqrt{45^2-30^2}=15\sqrt5\text{ m}\\s_{40}&=\sqrt{45^2-40^2}=5\sqrt{17}\text{ m}\\S_{30}&=\frac{\alpha}{360^{\circ}}\pi(45)^2-\frac12(30)(15\sqrt5)\\S_{40}&=\frac{\beta}{360^{\circ}}\pi(45)^2-\frac12(40)(5\sqrt{17})\\A_{\text{accessible}}&=\frac14\pi(45)^2-S_{30}-S_{40}\\A_{\text{accessible}}&\approx1172.444332\text{ m}^2\\\text{Percentage}&=\frac{A_{\text{accessible}}}{1200}\times100\\\text{Percentage}&\approx97.70\%.\end{align*}$$
